- White/cottony mycelium inside the stem cavity
- Dark black hard sclerotia (fungal bodies)
- Bleached/straw-colored stem exterior
- Stem splitting/shredding

This is strongly suggestive of White Mold (Sclerotinia stem rot). Let me verify with reference images.
Good match - black sclerotia on bleached stem. Let me check another White Mold reference to confirm the interior view.
Good - white cottony mycelium and dark sclerotia visible. Now let me check Charcoal Rot to differentiate.
Phomopsis shows pod/seed damage - different from the test image. One more reference needed.

Fusarium shows stem curling - clearly different.

**Analysis summary:**
- Test image: split soybean stem with **white cottony mycelium** and **large black sclerotia** inside the pith cavity — hallmark features of Sclerotinia stem rot (White Mold)
- White Mold references 133 and 415 both show the exact same combination: bleached/shredded stem, white mycelium, black sclerotia
- Charcoal Rot: only tiny embedded microsclerotia, no white mycelium, field-level wilting
- Phomopsis: pod/seed damage pattern
- Fusarium: stem curling/crown rot pattern

The large black sclerotia + white cottony mycelium inside a split bleached stem is definitively White Mold.
